question: kappa(theta) = least order of a tree carrying a nowhere-vanishing theta-eigenvector
why: BGM Lemma 4.2 forces every component of a theta-Aomoto subset to be such a tree, so kappa(theta)*cc(G[S]) <= |S| replaces the crude |S| >= 2 cc(G[S]) in the degree-spread chain, giving Delta > (delta-2) kappa(theta) + 2.
method: exhaustive over all trees on n vertices by Prufer sequence with dedup on (spectrum, degree sequence); an eigenvalue qualifies iff some vector in its eigenspace is nonzero at every vertex, tested as min over i of the norm of row i of an orthonormal eigenspace basis > 1e-7
pattern: the running minimum drops only at even n = 2m and equals 2 cos(m pi/(2m+1)) = 2 sin(pi/(2(2m+1))), attained by the path P_{2m} at k = m, which qualifies because gcd(m, 2m+1) = 1

refuted_predictions.P83a: REFUTED for odd n. The minimum over trees of order exactly n is attained by a path only for even n; at n = 5, 7, 9 a non-path tree beats every path.
refuted_predictions.P83b: REFUTED in the same way. The gcd formula min over gcd(k,n+1)=1 of |2 cos(k pi/(n+1))| gives the correct value only for even n.

surviving_claim: the RUNNING minimum, over all trees of order at most n, is the path value at the largest even order, and is unaffected by the odd-order failures because odd orders never improve on the preceding even order
conjecture: kappa(theta) >= 2m whenever |theta| < 2 cos(m pi/(2m+1)); verified exhaustively for all trees of order at most 9, i.e. for m <= 4
asymptotic: 2 sin(pi/(2(2m+1))) ~ pi/(n+1), so kappa(theta) is about pi/|theta|
not_formalized: the path eigenvector formula (classical) and the conjecture (a conjecture)
